role: Fine-pitch pads and copper escape examiner

directChecks.check: Native electrical pad geometry and logical identity
directChecks.details: Parsed real rounded/rectangular/polygonal pads, actual orientations, plated hole layers, and drilled copper. All connectivity keys resolve to exactly one source graph root; no unassigned electrical primitives.

directChecks.check: Imported fine-pitch footprint dimensions in emitted geometry
directChecks.details: U_PD has 25 pads, including 0.25 x 0.60 mm lead lands; U2 has 21 pads, including 0.45 x 1.05 mm lands; U_MCU has 20 pads, including rotated 1.35 x 0.40 mm lands; U_INPUT has 10 real copper pads with polygonal corner/power lands. Their emitted copper geometry was included directly instead of bounding rectangles.

strengths: No foreign trace-pad, via-pad, or pad-pad copper overlap was found in the exact capture.
Fine-pitch escapes retain about 0.20 mm or greater foreign-net separation; there is no sub-0.10 mm squeeze-through shortcut.
Corrected imported polygon and rotated pad geometry is respected and every electrical pad joins its expected physical net.
No ambiguous source-net key was needed to excuse a geometric intersection.

findings.explanation: Several trace-to-foreign-pad separations sit exactly on the 0.20 mm nominal design target. This is connected, non-overlapping copper, but leaves little extra design margin for later edits in crowded escape regions. In roomy regions, moving the non-pad trace farther away would strengthen the design. It is not a confirmed short or a demonstrated fabrication failure.

A GND via beside R21 TEC_HIGH_GATE has 0.200569 mm pad clearance, only 0.000569 mm beyond the 0.20 mm target. It passes the measured geometric threshold. A little more placement margin would make the gate region easier to edit and inspect; this does not itself imply an electrical fault.

suspectedShortAssessment.conclusion: No confirmed foreign-net short involving an electrical pad in this capture.
suspectedShortAssessment.scope: Whole-board pad-versus-trace, pad-versus-via, and foreign pad-versus-pad geometry, checked on shared physical layers only.
suspectedShortAssessment.screenshotSpecific: The supplied crop alone does not establish the identities or copper layers of its crossing lines. I did not independently localize that crop; trace-to-trace and trace-to-via checks belong to the other reviewers. Therefore this result does not clear a possible line-to-line crossing in the crop.

topImprovements: Where the component placement permits, increase non-pad copper clearance beyond 0.20 mm instead of repeatedly resting on the minimum target.
Move the GND via next to R21 outward slightly if an unchanged return path can be retained.
Keep fine-pitch lead widths and polygonal power lands intact while making any route refinements; do not substitute a generic imported footprint.
limitations: Score is for ideal static pad escape routing. It does not accept manufacturing, mask/stencil choices, or hardware behavior.
Reuse of the audited native continuity shape routines is explicit; the added all-foreign-net pair scans are independent of existing PASS receipts.
Copper circles and strokes use high-resolution polygon approximations. Distances at a few nanometres around a threshold are not meaningful manufacturing tolerance estimates.
Only electrical pads with source-port identities were included. Decorative copper and mechanical mounting copper are outside this assigned scope.
No changes to source, runtime, routing capture, or existing review artifacts were made.
